title: Put the Dungeon in the Bag (again) (Bag of Dungeon 2)
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ao4VRNX_h4A

Daniel (@dungeondive) reckons Gunpowder Studios have quietly cornered the light, breezy, small-box crawl, and that Bag of Dungeon 2: The Cursed Forest might be their best — a review copy, minis included, which he's passing to a patron because he prefers the wooden meeples.

The forest is drawn tile by tile as before, but this one leans co-operative. *Tagging* costs an action to haul another hero into your fight, and early on it's often the only way anything dies. The eight heroes carry that weight: a rogue who outright kills on doubles, a hunter whose crossbows never break, Moonbeam the fairy with a once-per-combat psionic blast who gets shoved out of her square whenever she's hit, a wizard paying health for spells, and a changeling who three times can wear the shape of something she killed.

Poison is the clever cruelty — it fills inventory slots rather than simply hurting, so a poisoned hero is a disarmed one. You hunt four brood seeds, each granting its bearer a power, then lay out the entire forest to find the tree and plant them, at which point the boss arrives. Solo gives each hero a single life, which he likens to an arcade run; he hasn't won yet.

He closes with a daydream: splice Seven Moons' overland map onto both Bags of Dungeon and play one long campaign across all three.

----

Daniel wants to repurpose one game's map as the connective tissue for two others. Have you ever cannibalised games you own into a bigger one?
